title: Longest Valid Parentheses
description:
# Longest Valid Parentheses

Given a string `s` containing only the characters `'('` and `')'`, return the length of the longest contiguous substring that is a valid parentheses string.

A valid parentheses string is well formed: every opening parenthesis is matched by a later closing parenthesis, and every prefix has at least as many opening parentheses as closing parentheses.

## Example 1:

**Input:** s = "(()"
**Output:** 2
**Explanation:** The longest valid parentheses substring is "()".

## Example 2:

**Input:** s = ")()())"
**Output:** 4
**Explanation:** The longest valid parentheses substring is "()()".

## Example 3:

**Input:** s = ""
**Output:** 0

## Constraints:

*   `0 <= s.length <= 3 * 10^4`
*   `s[i]` is `'('` or `')'`.

tests.description: only the last two characters form a valid pair
invalid prefix and suffix should not block the middle valid substring
empty string has no parentheses to match
adjacent and nested valid parts merge into the whole string
a reset is needed after an unmatched closing parenthesis
nested balanced group spans the whole string
unfinished opening parentheses at the end must be ignored
long valid prefix followed by one extra closing parenthesis
valid suffix after an early invalid close must still be found
several adjacent pairs form one valid substring

solutions.name: Stack with Sentinel Index
solutions.description:
## Approach

Use a stack of indices. Start with `-1` as the base before the current valid region. Push every `'('` index. For each `')'`, pop one index; if the stack becomes empty, push the current index as the new invalid base, otherwise update the answer with `i - stack.peek()`.

## Key Insight

The top of the stack after a successful match is the index just before the current valid suffix. Subtracting it from the current index gives the length of the longest valid substring ending here.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)

solutions.name: Dynamic Programming Ending at Each Index
solutions.description:
## Approach

Let `dp[i]` be the length of the longest valid parentheses substring ending exactly at index `i`. Only a closing parenthesis can end a valid substring. Handle the simple `...()` case and the nested or chained `...))` case by jumping back over `dp[i - 1]`.

## Key Insight

When `s[i]` is `')'` and the character before the previous valid suffix is `'('`, that matching pair can wrap the previous suffix and also connect to a valid substring before it.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)

solutions.name: Two-Pass Counter Scan
solutions.description:
## Approach

Scan left to right while counting opening and closing parentheses. Reset when closing parentheses become too many. Then scan right to left and reset when opening parentheses become too many. Equal counts in either direction give a valid length.

## Key Insight

A single left-to-right pass misses suffixes with extra opening parentheses, and a single right-to-left pass misses prefixes with extra closing parentheses. The two directions cover both imbalance types without a stack.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(1)

solutions.name: Mark Matched Pairs then Scan
solutions.description:
## Approach

Use a stack to match pairs of parentheses. Whenever a `')'` matches an earlier `'('`, mark both positions as valid in a boolean array. Finally scan the boolean array for the longest consecutive run of marked positions.

## Key Insight

A valid parentheses substring consists exactly of positions that can be partitioned into matched pairs with no gaps. Marking all matched positions turns the problem into finding the longest contiguous block of matched characters.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)
